claim: The new proof of `Finset.mem_map_equiv` (`simp only [mem_map, Equiv.coe_toEmbedding]` then `grind`) is a golf that makes this basic `@[simp 1100]` lemma slower: the PR's own profile reports <10 ms before and 25 ms after. It also still needs the `simp only` step, because `grind` alone fails here. A one-line `simp` proof exists that uses no `grind`.
requested_change: Replace the proof body of `Finset.mem_map_equiv` with `by simp [Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply]`, or revert this declaration to its previous proof. Do not keep a change that regresses the timing.
evidence: PR description: `Finset.mem_map_equiv`: <10 ms before, 25 ms after. lean_verify_edit on Mathlib/Data/Finset/Image.lean: the file as the PR leaves it compiles. The replacement `simp [Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply]` gives success=true with no warnings. So does `simp only [mem_map, Equiv.coe_toEmbedding, Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply, exists_eq_right]`. Plain `grind` fails, and so do `grind [Equiv.coe_toEmbedding]` and `grind [Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply]`: grind cannot close `f.toEmbedding w = b ⊢ f.symm b ∈ s`. Bare `simp` leaves `(∃ a ∈ s, f a = b) ↔ f.symm b ∈ s`.
